metadata.case_name: CHAN SIU YIM v. DR CHEUNG SHEUNG KIN ALSO KNOWN AS DR SAMUEL KINNETH CHEUNG

injuries.description: extraction of the lower left first pre-molar (tooth 34)
source: At the appointment that took place on 13 December 2007, without any prior notice to the plaintiff and without the plaintiff’s consent, the defendant extracted the lower left first pre-molar (“tooth 34”) from the plaintiff.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of hard dental tissues and pulp

injuries.description: occlusion problems including increased overjet and worsening centreline discrepancy (malocclusion / worsened occlusion)
source: A number of problems emerged after the commencement of the treatment, including occlusion problem which affected her chewing; upper teeth displaced and shifted to the left and overjet of the upper teeth increased.
After receiving the defendant’s treatment, the plaintiff had an overjet of 3.5mm while the overjet had been 1-2mm before the treatment commenced.

The centerline was worsened with the lower moving further to the left. Before receiving treatment by the defendant, the centerline had been shifted to the left by 2mm, and when the plaintiff began to receive remedial treatment from Dr Tong, her midline of the lower jaw was off to the left by 4mm.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of teeth or supporting structures

injuries.description: adjustment disorder with anxiety and depressed mood (psychiatric injury)
source: the dental problems caused by the defendant’s treatment also caused her to have serious headache, insomnia and depressive mood. As a result of these, she consulted a psychiatrist in the Prince of Wales Hospital, and was diagnosed with adjustment disorder with insomnia.
The plaintiff is suffering from adjustment disorder with anxiety and depressed mood, which is caused by the unsatisfactory dental treatment from 2007 to 2010.

At the appointment that took place on 13 December 2007, without any prior notice to the plaintiff and without the plaintiff’s consent, the defendant extracted the lower left first pre-molar (“tooth 34”) from the plaintiff.

treatments_received.treatment: application of brackets and wire to the plaintiff’s upper teeth
source: The defendant applied brackets and wire to the plaintiff’s upper teeth as well to try to remedy the situation.

treatments_received.treatment: remedial orthodontic treatment by Dr Tong (30 sessions)
source: On or about 17 November 2010, the plaintiff was not able to bear with the problem anymore and consulted Dr Winston Tong (“Dr Tong”), an orthodontics specialist, for a second opinion. Dr Tong took the plaintiff as his patient in January 2011.
After 30 sessions of treatment by Dr Tong, the whole remedial process was completed in August 2012.

treatments_received.treatment: psychiatric treatment including prescription of anti-depressant and benzodiazepine
source: As a result of these, she consulted a psychiatrist in the Prince of Wales Hospital, and was diagnosed with adjustment disorder with insomnia. She was prescribed with anti-depressant and benzodiazepine.

treatments_future.treatment: psychological as well as psychiatric treatment for another 6 months
source: The plaintiff should continue receive psychological as well as psychiatric treatment for another 6 months after this case is settled.
When this case is over, the plaintiff should continue receive psychological and psychiatric treatment for another 6 months. The costs of the treatment would be about HK$25,000 in the private sector.

losses.description: Loss of the lower left first pre-molar (tooth 34) following extraction.

losses.category: Loss of ability to enjoy food and drink
losses.description: Unable to chew properly due to occlusion problem and displacement of teeth.
Slurring of speech affecting the plaintiff's speech.
Affected facial appearance as a result of the dental problems.
The plaintiff says the treatment contributed to the breaking up of the relationship between her and her boyfriend.

comparable_cases.case_name: Wong Yuen Mei v Young Yau Yau Cecilia
comparable_cases.injury_description: defendant dentist who extracted 4 first pre-molars of the plaintiff. The extraction caused the plaintiff the problems of unfit upper teeth with lower teeth; ulcer of gum, headache, depression, anxiety and insomnia, incapable of making oral announcement as a flight attendant; could not chew properly; loss of weight and appetite; and after a series of remedial treatments, the plaintiff had decreased longevity of the teeth and increased risk of tooth decay.

comparable_cases.case_name: Mak Po Ling v Young Yau Yau Cecilia
comparable_cases.injury_description: the defendant dentist extracted three teeth and she experienced similar problems including issues with chewing, headache, depression, anxiety and insomnia; the plaintiff’s condition had significantly improved after remedial treatment.
